rows.subtopic: Caste and class awareness, discrimination recognition and fair conduct
rows.description: A young adult forms a close bond across caste and faces relatives' worry or anger. Patience, honesty and standing by the friend or partner matter more than winning the family argument in one go.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: affection, anger, anxiety

rows.description: A child notices that a friend prays differently or wears different clothes and asks why. Simple honest answers such as they have their own way of praying keep curiosity open and free of fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child shares food on Eid, Diwali or Christmas with neighbours and feels part of something bigger than one home. Small gestures like these make later prejudice harder to believe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager hears jokes or rumours about their religion from classmates or media and feels angry, ashamed or silenced. Friends who speak up and adults who name the stereotype as false give real protection.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager finds a close friend of another faith pulling away after a news event or a family warning. Staying in touch, asking honestly and refusing to blame the friend for others' acts keeps trust alive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult attends a friend's prayer or service to learn, without any wish to change belief. Asking respectfully and following local etiquette shows interest and honours the difference.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, curiosity, interest

rows.description: A parent worries when a child has close friends or a partner of another faith, fearing social talk or loss of tradition. Honest conversation about values, not labels, usually helps more than banning friendships.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A couple from different faiths negotiates names, rites and children's upbringing while facing both families' worry. Clear early talks and mutual respect matter more than winning any single rule.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Standing beside a neighbour under threat [Response]
rows.description: A young adult offers company, help or a voice when a neighbour of another faith faces hostility. Simple solidarity, without stoking anger at anyone else, is a practical and human answer.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child asks whether God is real and gets very different answers at home and at school. Honest, calm replies that say people believe differently protect curiosity and trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: curiosity, calm, trust
